summary_en: ND-net is a progressive two-branch reconstruction framework for highly sparse-view photoacoustic computed tomography. A residual branch first estimates structured sparse-view artifacts, and an adversarially guided diffusion branch then restores full-view structure. The design supports large reverse steps and requires only four diffusion iterations, with validation on simulated vessels, phantom measurements, and in vivo mouse-abdomen imaging.

summary_en: This work establishes an effective point-spread-function model for photoacoustic remote sensing microscopy, showing that resolution is jointly governed by the excitation and probe optical paths. The authors validate the model numerically and experimentally with a multipath confocal PARS platform and demonstrate controlled PSF contraction that approximately doubles axial resolution. It is a direct acoustic-optics imaging and system-design contribution.

summary_en: RT-FWI combines Radon-domain separation of scalp-related multiple reflections with spatially regularized elastic full-waveform inversion to address two major transcranial PACT degradations simultaneously. In simulation and ex vivo validation, the method improves axial resolution from 1.14 mm to 0.28 mm and SSIM from 0.415 to 0.875 relative to the reported baselines. It is a strong physics-based photoacoustic reconstruction paper.

summary_en: This paper introduces an acousto-optic-modulator-based interferometric excitation scheme for frequency-domain photoacoustic microscopy. The approach keeps the modulation frequencies within the narrow resonance of a high-Q ultrasound transducer while preserving simultaneous dual-wavelength acquisition, improving the reliability of functional oxygen-saturation imaging. It is directly relevant to photoacoustic and acousto-optic imaging instrumentation.
